questions.question: Which of the following is **NOT **included in the value added method of calculating national income?

options.text: Value of final goods and services produced in economy
All value of producing enterprises in primary sector

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Value of second-hand goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Value Added Method**

 
 
• In a circular flow,** national income** is calculated using the **value-added method **at various phases of the production process. In the production process, it indicates the** value added for each unit produced**.
 
• Every business **adds value to the goods** it purchases as an intermediary good from other firms.
 
• The value of **national income** is the** sum total of value added by all organisations**.
 
• The** following steps are used to calculate national income** using the value-added method:
 
 
• **Step 1**
 
• The first step is to **identify and classify** all value of producing enterprises in ** primary, secondary, and tertiary sectors**.
 
• **Step 2**
 
• Next, the **Gross Domestic Product at Market Prices (GDPMP)** is calculated.
 
• Determine the Gross Value Added at Market Price (GVAMP) of each sector for the purpose of calculating the GDPMP; **i.e. ∑GVAMP = GDPMP**
 
• **Step 3**
 
• Next, determine domestic income (NDPFC).
 
• **Value of depreciation and net indirect tax **are deducted from the gross domestic product at market price (GDPMP) to calculate domestic income; **NDPFC = GDPMP – Depreciation – Net Indirect Taxes**
 
• **Step 4**
 
• To determine national income **(NNPFC**), the final step is to calculate** Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA)**.
 
• The NFIA is added along with the country's domestic income; **National Income or NNPFC = Domestic Income or NDPFC + NFIA**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Value Added**

 
 
• Value-added describes the **value that a company adds to a raw material or intermediate good** during the production process.
 
• The difference between the** value of output and the value of intermediate products** is used to calculate the national income using the value-added method.
 
 

** Value Added = Value of Output – Intermediate Consumption **

 
• The value-added method, prevents double counting, which is a major mistake while calculating national income, and therefore this method is most frequently used to estimate national income.
 
• **Value of second-hand goods should not be considered in national income because they are already valued in the year they were manufactured**. The current flow of goods and services will be disrupted if the value of these goods is added again.

questions.question: Identify the true statement among the following.

options.text: Income Tax is an Indirect Tax
Goods and Services Tax is a direct tax
Fees and Fines collected is a non-tax receipt
Borrowings from the public is a revenue receipt

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fees and Fines collected is a non-tax receipts.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fees and fines** collected are considered **non-tax receipts** because they are **not imposed **as a result of any legislative power or authority.
 
• The government's recurring income from sources **other than taxes** is known as** non-tax revenue.**
 
• These are the taxes collected that do not originate from **levies **on the general populace.
 
• Payments received that** do not** give rise to** liabilities or a claim **against the government are known as revenue receipts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income tax** is a tax levied on the income earned by an individual or entity.

 
 
• It is a **direct tax **as it is levied on the** income of the taxpayer.**
 
 
 
• **Goods and Services Tax** (GST) is a tax imposed on the **supply of goods and services.**
 
 
• It is an **indirect tax** as it is** not levied directly **on the income of the taxpayer.
 
 
 
• **Borrowings** from the public are a form of **external debt**.
 
 
• The government borrows from the **public to finance** its developmental activities.
 
• It is a **capital receipt **as it** does not **generate regular income for the government.

questions.question: _____ at Market Price refers to the sum total of factor incomes earned by residents of a country during an accounting year including net indirect taxes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net National Product (NNP)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** at Market Price refers to the sum total of factor incomes earned by residents of a country during an accounting year including net indirect taxes.
 
• It is derived by subtracting depreciation from Gross National Product (GNP).
 
• It represents the net value of goods and services produced by the residents of a country.
 
• NNP is an important indicator of the economic health of a country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The calculation of NNP takes into account the depreciation of capital assets, making it a more accurate measure of economic performance than Gross National Product (GNP).
 
• Net National Product (NNP) can be used to gauge the standard of living within a country, as it reflects the actual income available to the residents.
 
• It is also used for international comparisons of economic performance.
 
• Depreciation represents the wear and tear on the capital stock, which is why it is deducted from the Gross National Product to arrive at the Net National Product.
 
• Higher NNP indicates a higher level of economic activity and prosperity within a country.

questions.question:
Match the items is List I with those in List II.

 
 

 
 **Measure of National Income**
 
 **Formula**
 
 

 i.
 GNP
 a.
 GNP - Depreciation
 
 

 ii.
 NNP
 b.
 C + I + G + Net exports
 
 

 iii.
 GDP
 c.

 iv.
 NDP
 d.

options.text: i - b, ii - d, iii - a, iv - c
i - a, ii - c, iii - d, iv - b
i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c
i - c, ii - b, iii - d, iv - a

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** i - d, ii - a, iii - b, iv - c.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GNP:-**

 
 
• Gross National Product is the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents, including those produced abroad, and can be calculated as C (consumption) + I (investment) + G (government spending) + net exports (exports - imports).
 
 
 
• **NNP:-**
 
 
• (Net National Product) is the GNP minus depreciation, which is the decrease in value of capital goods over time due to wear and tear.
 
 
 
• **GDP:-**
 
 
• (Gross Domestic Product) is the total value of goods and services produced within a country's borders, and can be calculated as C + I + G + net exports.
 
 
 
• **NDP:-**
 
 
• (Net Domestic Product) is the GDP minus depreciation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National income measures:-**

 
 
• These are important indicators of a country's economic performance and are used for policy-making and analysis.
 
• Another measure of national income is GNI (Gross National Income), which is similar to GNP but includes net income from abroad and excludes net taxes and subsidies.
 
• Per capita measures of national income, such as GDP per capita or GNP per capita, can provide insights into the standard of living of a country's population.
 
• National income measures have limitations and do not capture important aspects of economic activity, such as non-market activities, informal sector, and environmental degradation.

questions.question:
In the given expression of GDP according to the expenditure method, which of the following represents the aggregate imports expenditure incurred by the economy?

C + I + G + X - M
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M**__**__.__**​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Point__**

Expenditure method of income measurement:

__
 
• The expenditure method is a system for calculating gross domestic product (GDP) that combines C + I + G + X - M where *consumption (C), investment(I), government spending(G), and net exports(X-M) where M is import and X is export.*
 
• It is the most common way to estimate GDP. It says everything that the private sector, including consumers and private firms, and government spending within the borders of a particular country, must add up to the total value of all finished goods and services produced over a certain period of time. This method produces nominal GDP, which must then be adjusted for inflation to result in the real GDP.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Product Method:

 
 
• The product or value-added method is a way of computing the national income of a country.
 
• This system is also known as the output or inventory method. This method calculates national income by adding value to a product at every stage of its production.
 
 
 
• Income Method:
 
 
• In the income method, the national income is measured by adding up the pretax income generated by the individuals and companies in the economy.
 
• It consists of income from wages, rent of buildings and land, interest on capital, profits, etc.

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the National Income?

I. Intermediate goods are not included in the calculation of national income.

II. Final goods are included in the calculation of national income.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is *__**Both I and II.**__*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****National Income Calculation**

__
 
• **Intermediate goods** are not included in the calculation of national income.

 
 
• Intermediate goods are products used in the production of final goods and services. Including them would result in double counting, as their value is already embedded in the value of final goods.
 
 ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Final goods** are included in the calculation of national income.
 
 
• Final goods are products that have completed the production process and are available for consumption or investment. These goods are counted in national income because they reflect the actual value of production in the economy.
 
 ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Income Overview**

 
 
• National income is a measure of the total value of goods and services produced by a country within a specific period, typically one year.
 
• It is calculated using various methods, including the income method, production method, and expenditure method.
 
 
 
• **Exclusion of Intermediate Goods**
 
 
• Excluding intermediate goods prevents double counting and ensures that only the value of final products is considered, providing a more accurate measure of economic output.
 
 
 
• **Inclusion of Final Goods**
 
 
• Final goods are included in national income calculations because they represent the end product of economic activity, reflecting the actual value created in the economy.
 
 

Key facts about National income in India-

 
• The first attempt to calculate the national income of India was made by Dadabhai Naoroji.
 
• The first scientific method for calculating national income was made by Prof. V.K.R.V. Rao in 1931 but was not satisfactory.
 
• The first official attempt was made by National Income Committee headed by Prof. P.C. Mahalanobis in 1949.
 
• *Central Statistical Organization (CSO)* is responsible for calculating National income in India.

questions.question: If there is a fall in the demand of a good, the equilibrium price is expected to:

options.text: first rise, and then fall sharply

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fall**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When there is a fall in the demand for a good, the equilibrium price is expected to **fall**.
 
• The equilibrium price is determined by the intersection of the demand and supply curves. A decrease in demand shifts the demand curve to the left.
 
• This shift results in a new equilibrium where the quantity demanded and supplied are lower, leading to a lower price.
 
• Other factors being constant, a fall in demand reduces the competition for the good, causing sellers to lower prices to attract buyers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity of a good demanded by consumers equals the quantity supplied by producers.
 
• A shift in the demand or supply curve can lead to a new equilibrium price and quantity.
 
• Factors that can cause a fall in demand include a decrease in consumer income, changes in tastes and preferences, and the availability of substitutes.
 
• Understanding the dynamics of demand and supply is crucial for predicting market behavior and making informed economic decisions.

questions.question:
Consider the given consumption function of country X and answer the following question.

C = 100 + 0.8Y

What is the value of autonomous consumption (A) and marginal propensity to consume (MPC) in the given equation?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer** A = 100, MPC = 0.8**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

The **consumption function** you provided is in the form of a **simple linear equation:**

 
• **C = A + MPC*Y**

where:

 
• **C represents consumption,**
 
• **A represents autonomous consumption,**
 
• **MPC represents the marginal propensity to consume, and**
 
• **Y represents income.**

Comparing this with your given function **C = 100 + 0.8Y, **we can identify the values of** A and MPC.**

 
• **A (Autonomous consumption)** is part of **consumption that occurs when income is zero.**
 
• It's the intercept of the consumption function on the consumption axis.
 
• This is represented by the constant term in the equation, which in this case is **100.**
 
• **MPC (Marginal Propensity to Consume) **is the change in consumption resulting from a **one-unit change in income.**
 
• It's the slope of the **consumption function.**
 
• In your given function, this is represented** by 0.8.**

So, in the given consumption function C = 100 + 0.8Y, autonomous consumption (A) is 100 and the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is 0.8.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a transfer payment?

a) Unemployment allowances

b) Scholarships

c) Retirement pension

options.text: All of a, b and c

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of a, b and c**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A transfer payment **is a payment made by a government for which no goods or services are received in return.
 
• **Unemployment allowances:**
 
 
• This is a transfer payment because it is typically provided by the government to individuals who are unemployed and seeking employment.
 
• No goods or services are exchanged directly for this payment.
 
 
 
• **Scholarships:**
 
 
• While scholarships are payments made to individuals, they are often made by organizations, institutions, or individuals themselves, rather than directly by the government.
 
• Scholarships are typically awarded to support education and are often based on merit, need, or some other criteria. As such, they may not always be classified as transfer payments, especially if they are funded privately.
 
 
 
• **Retirement pension:**
 
 
• It is a form of **deferred compensation** for services already rendered by employees during their working years.
 
• Therefore, it is considered an **earned benefit** rather than a transfer payment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• A transfer payment is a redistribution of wealth and income that occurs when the government pays for something without expecting anything in return, such as products or services.
 
• Since these payments don't directly use resources or produce output, they are regarded as non-exhaustive.
 
• Welfare, financial aid, social security, and government subsidies for certain industries are a few examples of transfer payments.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about GDP and Welfare are correct?

1) GDP of a country is a indicator of welfare of the people.

2) If GDP is rising, the welfare may not rise equally.

3) GDP and Welfare both are not related each other.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GDP as an Indicator of Welfare:** GDP (Gross Domestic Product) of a country is often used as an **indicator of the economic health** and a proxy for the welfare of the people. It reflects the total value of goods and services produced over a specific time period within a nation. A higher GDP usually suggests better living standards and economic stability. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **GDP Growth and Welfare:** Even if GDP is rising, it does not necessarily mean that the welfare of all people is rising equally. The benefits of GDP growth might not be evenly distributed among the population. For instance,** income inequality, environmental degradation, and other social factors can affect overall welfare despite GDP growth**. ***Hence, Statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Relation Between GDP and Welfare:** GDP and welfare are related, but they are not the same. GDP measures economic activity, while welfare encompasses a broader range of factors including health, education, and overall quality of life. Therefore, it is incorrect to say that GDP and welfare are not related at all. ***Hence, Statement 3 is not correct.***

Based on the above points, the correct answer is **Only 1 and 2**__.

questions.question: The collection of all bundles that the consumer can buy with her income at the prevailing market prices is called the _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Budget set**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The collection of all bundles that the consumer can buy with her income at the prevailing market prices is called the Budget set.
 
• The budget set represents all the combinations of goods and services that the consumer can afford given the prices and their income.
 
• This set is subject to the budget constraint, which is the limitation on the consumer's income that they cannot surpass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Budget constraint:**

 
 
• **​**A budget constraint represents the limit on the consumption bundles that a consumer can afford.
 
• It is a line that maps out every combination of goods and services that a consumer can purchase if they spend all of their income.
 
• The budget constraint is determined by the consumer's income, the price of one good, and the price of the other good.
 
 
 
• **Budget anomaly:**
 
 
• **​**This term isn't commonly used in the field of economics.
 
• An "anomaly" typically refers to something that deviates from the norm or from expectations.
 
• In the context of a budget, it could hypothetically refer to an unexpected or unusual occurrence in relation to the budget, but it's not a standard term you'd find in economic theory or analysis.
 
 
 
• **Budget line:**
 
 
• **​**This is another term for the budget constraint.
 
• It's a graphical representation of all the combinations of goods that a consumer can afford with a given income, given the prices of those goods.
 
• The budget line shows the boundary of the budget set.
 
• If prices or income change, the budget line will shift.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are FALSE?

A) The impact of externality is always positive.

B) Real national income means national income at constant prices
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **externality** refers to the occurrence of a cost or benefit resulting from the actions of one party, yet borne or enjoyed financially by another.
 
• These effects may impact individuals or entire organizations and can be classified as either private or societal.
 
• **Positive externalities** arise when they provide a benefit to a third party. For instance, the construction of infrastructure like flyovers or highways can decrease transportation expenses and travel duration for users.
 
• Conversely, negative externalities occur when they impose a cost on third parties. For example, the construction of roads may lead to erosion and chemical runoff, subsequently polluting water sources downstream. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real national income, **also referred to as national income at constant prices, denotes the total income of a country adjusted for inflation.
 
• This measure, also known as nominal or money national income, reflects the actual purchasing power of a currency at a particular juncture.
 
• Constant prices, representing real value, are adjusted for price fluctuations concerning a baseline or reference point.
 
• In contrast, current prices, denoting nominal value, are those prevailing at a specific moment.
 
• Real national income offers a more precise evaluation of the real shifts in production and economic activity over time, enhancing the accuracy of comparisons.

• It is one of the most important indicators of a country's economic health.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies**:-
 
 
• A subsidy is a financial benefit given by a government to a producer or consumer of a good or service.
 
• Subsidies can be direct or indirect. Direct subsidies are payments made to the producer or consumer, while indirect subsidies are tax breaks or other benefits that reduce the cost of production or consumption.
 
 
 
• **Indirect tax:-**
 
 
• **It is a tax that is levied on the consumption of goods and services. **
 
• It is not directly levied on the income of a person.

questions.question:
While using the income method to compute national income, which of the following is NOT to be included?

A) Income from lottery

B) Brokerage on sale and purchase of shares

C) Income from illegal activities like gambling
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A and C.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Income method:-**

 
 
• It is one of the methods used to calculate national income.
 
• It involves adding up all the incomes earned by individuals and businesses in the economy. 
 
 
 
• **Lottery income:-**
 
 
• It is considered a windfall gain and is not a regular source of income.
 
• It is not a productive activity and does not contribute to the production of goods and services in the economy.
 
• Therefore, income from lottery is not included while calculating national income using the income method.
 
 
 
• **Brokerage on sale and purchase of shares:-**
 
 
• Brokerage income is earned by individuals or firms that facilitate the buying and selling of shares in the stock market.
 
• This income is a result of productive activity and is included while calculating national income using the income method.
 
 
 
• **Income from illegal activities like gambling:-**
 
 
• Income earned from illegal activities like gambling is not included in the calculation of national income.
 
• Such activities are not recognized by the government and are not considered productive activities that contribute to the economy

questions.question: Gross Domestic Product less Depreciation is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Net Domestic Product**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Domestic Product:**

 
 
• GDP is the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given time period.
 
 
 
• Depreciation is the decrease in value of an asset over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
 
• **NDP:-**
 
 
• It is a measure of the net output of the economy and is considered a more accurate indicator of economic growth than GDP.
 
• Gross Domestic Product less Depreciation is called Net Domestic Product (NDP). It represents the value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders minus the value of the capital goods (machinery, equipment, buildings, etc.) that were used up in the production process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Investment:-**

 
 
• It refers to the total amount of money spent on capital goods (machinery, equipment, buildings, etc.) within a country's borders in a given time period.
 
 
 
• **Net National Product:-**
 
 
• It is the value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents, including those living abroad, minus depreciation.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Product:-**
 
 
• It is the value of all goods and services produced by a country's residents, including those living abroad, without subtracting depreciation.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT the correctly stated component of the expenditure method of measuring national income?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Export plus import expenditure.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The expenditure method of measuring national income involves adding up the final expenditures made by households, firms, governments, and foreigners.
 
• Final investment expenditure by firms and final government expenditure are correctly stated components of the expenditure method.
 
• Final consumption expenditure by households is also a correctly stated component of the expenditure method.
 
• Export plus import expenditure, is a component of the expenditure method, but is NOT correctly stated. This should have been export-import expenditure, which is known as net exports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Final investment expenditure by firms:-**

 
 
• It refers to the amount spent by businesses on capital goods, such as machinery and equipment, that are used to produce goods and services.
 
 
 
• **Final government expenditure:-**
 
 
• It includes all spending by the government on goods and services, such as salaries of public employees and infrastructure projects.
 
 
 
• **Final consumption expenditure by households:-**
 
 
• It is the total amount spent by individuals and families on goods and services for personal use, such as food, clothing, and housing.
 
 
 
• **Net exports:-**
 
 
• These are the difference between the value of exports (goods and services sold to foreign countries) and imports (goods and services purchased from foreign countries).

questions.question: National income at constant prices means:

options.text: income estimated at base year prices
income estimated at any year prices
income estimated for next year prices
income estimated at current year prices

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**income estimated at base year prices**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Income estimated at base year prices** refers to national income calculated using the prices of a specific base year, which helps in eliminating the effects of inflation and provides a more accurate measure of real income over different periods.
 
• This method allows for a consistent comparison of economic performance over time by adjusting for changes in price levels.
 
• It is also known as** national income at constant prices or real national income**.
 
• Using base year prices helps in understanding the actual growth of the economy without the distortion caused by fluctuating prices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The concept of national income at constant prices is crucial for economic analysis and policy-making.
 
• It helps in understanding the real growth of different sectors of the economy.
 
• The base year is periodically updated to reflect more recent economic conditions and to provide a more accurate measure of real economic performance.
 
• National income is a vital indicator of the economic health of a country and is used for planning and development purposes.
 
• Organizations like the** Central Statistical Office (CSO)** in India are responsible for calculating and publishing national income data.
